sc: 6-week-old, sweating and breathless on feeds, pansystolic murmur, big liver → Large VSD with heart failure
Well school child, soft ejection murmur, wide fixed split S2 → Secundum ASD
Child with headache, high BP in the arms, weak delayed femoral pulses → Coarctation of the aorta
f: Commonest CHD (30%) · pansystolic murmur lower left sternal edge · small = loud, often closes · large: heart failure at 6–8 weeks
Ejection murmur upper left sternal edge (flow) · wide fixed split S2 · primum: left axis deviation · device closure
Preterm, rubella · continuous machinery murmur below left clavicle · bounding pulses · ibuprofen (preterm) or device closure
Weak, delayed femorals, high BP in arms · rib notching · Turner · neonatal shock when duct closes → PGE1
Furosemide + captopril, NG feeds · surgery for large VSD at 3–6 months
Heart failure · Eisenmenger (reversed shunt, cyanosis, softer murmur) · infective endocarditis
trap: In VSD the smallest defects make the loudest murmurs; a murmur getting softer with a loud P2 = pulmonary hypertension · ASD murmur is a flow murmur, not across the defect
